lines.trans: We are not giving up, guys, let us work fast and together!
Steaks on charcoal turn out even tastier.
Chef, the fridge is off, let me cook pilaf.
At least we will feed the kitchen today with this pilaf.
Go ahead and cook, just do not get underfoot.
Alright, Chef, a restaurant is nothing.
On our ship in the ocean all the generators failed.
Storyteller, look, all your fish is burning!
Once, Chef, we drifted for a whole month without fuel.
Then we refueled and calmly reached the shore.
Are you seriously telling me this right now?
Look, fire! All our meat has burned up!

examples.text: Однажды, шеф, мы целый месяц без топлива плыли.
examples.trans: Once, Chef, we drifted for a whole month without fuel.

examples.text: Я не могу гулять здесь целый день.
examples.trans: I can't walk around here all day.

examples.text: Мы ждали целый час.
examples.trans: We waited for a whole hour.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'month' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Однажды, шеф, мы целый месяц без топлива плыли.
examples.trans: Once, Chef, we drifted for a whole month without fuel.

examples.text: Я живу здесь месяц.
examples.trans: I've been living here for a month.

examples.text: Через месяц выборы.
examples.trans: The election is in a month.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'without', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Посмотрим, что тут самое безобидное.
examples.trans: Let us see what looks the most harmless in here.

examples.text: Однажды, шеф, мы целый месяц без топлива плыли.
examples.trans: Once, Chef, we drifted for a whole month without fuel.

examples.text: Видишь, я без денег больше никому не нужен.
examples.trans: You see, without money nobody needs me anymore.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'fuel' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Однажды, шеф, мы целый месяц без топлива плыли.
examples.trans: Once, Chef, we drifted for a whole month without fuel.

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть топливо.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always fuel.

meanings.en: to sail, swim, glide across water
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'sailed', paired with 'поплыть'.

examples.text: Однажды, шеф, мы целый месяц без топлива плыли.
examples.trans: Once, Chef, we drifted for a whole month without fuel.

examples.text: Дома ведь такие тёплые и уютные стены.
examples.trans: At home the walls are so warm and cozy.

examples.text: Белая яхта по морю плывёт.
examples.trans: A white yacht sails across the sea.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'then, afterwards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Этот человек всегда пытается тебя потрогать.
examples.trans: That person always tries to touch you.

examples.text: Потому что нас всех отсюда выгонят.
examples.trans: Because they will kick all of us out of here.

examples.text: Потому что крепкий кофе спать не даёт.
examples.trans: Because strong coffee does not let you sleep.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'правиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'refueled'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и заправиться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and refueled on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют заправиться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to refueled.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'покойно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Стой спокойно и красиво улыбайся.
examples.trans: Stand calmly and smile nicely.

examples.text: Потом заправились и спокойно дошли к берегу.
examples.trans: Then we refueled and calmly reached the shore.

examples.text: Лучше бы ты спокойно на природу пошёл.
examples.trans: You would have done better to go calmly into nature.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'reached', paired with 'доходить'.

examples.text: Извините, к вам скоро подойдёт официант.
examples.trans: Excuse me, a waiter will come to you soon.

examples.text: Но они, к сожалению, не дошли до вас.
examples.trans: But unfortunately, it never reached you.

examples.text: Мы быстро дошли до дома.
examples.trans: We quickly walked as far as the house.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'to, towards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Наш ресторан всегда остаётся лучшим в Москве.
examples.trans: Our restaurant always remains the best in Moscow.

examples.text: У нас работает команда профессиональных поваров.
examples.trans: A team of professional chefs works here.

examples.text: Здесь всегда продукты самого высокого качества.
examples.trans: There are always products of the highest quality here.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'shore' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Вот последняя банка, на, береги её.
examples.trans: Here is the last jar, take it and guard it.

examples.text: Береги эту последнюю банку.
examples.trans: Keep this last jar safe.

examples.text: Потом заправились и спокойно дошли к берегу.
examples.trans: Then we refueled and calmly reached the shore.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Давайте, ребята, сейчас не расслабляемся.
examples.trans: Come on, guys, let us not relax right now.

examples.text: А ты сейчас куда собрался, Сеня?
examples.trans: And where are you going right now, Senya?

examples.text: Максим, извините, что я сейчас вмешиваюсь.
examples.trans: Maxim, forgive me for interfering right now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ерьёзно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Вот это я сейчас серьёзно попал.
examples.trans: Now I have really gotten myself into trouble.

examples.text: Ты сейчас это серьёзно мне рассказываешь?
examples.trans: Are you seriously telling me this right now?

examples.text: Ты серьёзно?
examples.trans: Are you serious?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to me', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Наш ресторан всегда остаётся лучшим в Москве.
examples.trans: Our restaurant always remains the best in Moscow.

examples.text: Да мы сегодня не особо спешим.
examples.trans: We are not in much of a hurry today.

examples.text: В зале сегодня очень много заказов.
examples.trans: There are very many orders in the dining room today.

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'сказывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'tell', paired with 'рассказать'.

examples.text: Ты сейчас это серьёзно мне рассказываешь?
examples.trans: Are you seriously telling me this right now?

examples.text: Ну, рассказывай!
examples.trans: Well, tell me everything!

examples.text: Он рассказывает историю.
examples.trans: He's telling a story.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мотреть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'look', paired with 'посмотреть'.

examples.text: Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Look what I've got.

examples.text: Я смотрю телевизор.
examples.trans: I'm watching TV.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'flame' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Здесь всегда продукты самого высокого качества.
examples.trans: There are always products of the highest quality here.

examples.text: В зале сегодня очень много заказов.
examples.trans: There are very many orders in the dining room today.

examples.text: Сегодня у нас банкет для важного человека.
examples.trans: Today we have a banquet for an important man.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы всё прекрасно понимаем.
examples.trans: We understand everything perfectly.

examples.text: Я же в этот сейф всё отнёс!
examples.trans: I put everything into that safe!

examples.text: По всем признакам всё сходится.
examples.trans: By all the signs, everything adds up.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'meat' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Лёва поставит мясо в духовку надолго.
examples.trans: Lyova will put the meat in the oven for a long time.

examples.text: Смотрите, огонь! У нас всё мясо сгорело!
examples.trans: Look, fire! All our meat has burned up!

examples.text: А ты где мясо берёшь?
examples.trans: Where do you get your meat?

meanings.en: to burn up, to be destroyed by fire
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'гореть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'burned up', paired with 'сгорать'.

examples.text: Смотрите, огонь! У нас всё мясо сгорело!
examples.trans: Look, fire! All our meat has burned up!

examples.text: А трава в мешках сгорела.
examples.trans: And the herbs in the sacks burned.

examples.text: Тут пять килограммов сгорело!
examples.trans: Five kilograms burned here!
